preregistration: roadmap C benchmark ladder and comparison classes
frozen: 2026-09-08, BEFORE any C result was computed

supersedes.why: e5f779a defined L3 over precommitted schedules only and asserted a falsifier its class could not support. bb102d3 put the learner in the class and claimed the learner 'cannot beat L3 by construction'. THAT IS ALSO FALSE. Membership guarantees only that the learner CAN be selected on the selection stream; it does not guarantee that whichever member IS selected beats the learner on the independent evaluation stream, nor even in expectation at finite selection sample size. Selection noise can repeatedly choose a genuinely worse member. The mathematical property belongs to the population optimum; the observable quantity is an estimate, and the two were conflated.

schedule_class.note: unchanged from e5f779a; only the COMPARISON classes below are corrected

eligibility.rule: A schedule whose null calibration falls outside the declared +-30 % matched-E0[T] envelope is INELIGIBLE: it is excluded from selection and from every comparison, and named with its miss wherever a result reports the class.
eligibility.why: A policy outside the envelope is not held to the same false-alarm rate, so its delay ratio is not comparable. Leaving it in silently would let an incomparable number win or lose a selection. Roadmap B already has an instance: switch@300 at the pilot calibrates to +52.4 % after three repair attempts.
eligibility.predeclared: eligibility is decided by the calibration alone, never by the delay result

L2.name: best eligible robust precommitted schedule from roadmap B
L2.selection_rule: the eligible member of that four-schedule class with the SMALLEST worst-case delay ratio over tau_c in {20,5,1}, selected on the 700 + int(tau_c) + offset streams and evaluated on 200 + int(tau_c) + offset
L2.why_a_rule: 'best robust schedule from B' was underspecified and would have been chosen using B's own evaluation data, which is the selection bias this ladder exists to avoid
L2.licenses: whether posterior FEEDBACK adds value over scheduling WITHOUT feedback -- the minimum bar to move card item 4 out of the appendix

L3.name: tau_c-knowing finite-class benchmark over 12 eligible policies
L3.class: the eleven frozen schedules AND both learners, each identified by its SEED-FREE policy digest: greedy posterior-expected-rate (pilot fa22bac9ac38d6d7, stress 1778e8ebd51c92cb) and posterior sampling (pilot 3a687899c8b1821d, stress a8654d2ebc97a762)

target.what: the POPULATION finite-class optimum over the 12 eligible policies at each tau_c
target.property: includes the learner, so it is mathematically no worse than the learner. This is the only object with that property.
target.note: an estimand, not a measurement; nothing is reported as this

estimate.what: the member selected on the 700 + int(tau_c) + offset stream, evaluated on the 200 + int(tau_c) + offset stream
estimate.property: honest out-of-sample performance of a realisable selection procedure. It CAN lose to the learner through finite-sample selection error, and a resolved loss is a genuine finding about SELECTION INSTABILITY -- not necessarily a seed or implementation defect.
estimate.note: this is what a C result reports as L3

diagnostic_envelope.what: the minimum over all 12 candidates computed on the EVALUATION stream itself
diagnostic_envelope.property: cannot exceed the learner IN THAT SAMPLE, because the learner is one of the minimands. This is the only rung carrying a hard falsifier.
diagnostic_envelope.note: selected on the same noise it is scored on, so it is NOT deployable performance and must never be reported as achievable

L3.selection_rule: for each true tau_c independently, the eligible member with the smallest mean delay on the selection stream; measured on the evaluation stream
L3.licenses: A COMPARISON WITH AN INDEPENDENTLY SELECTED BENCHMARK. Not finite-class regret. The reported L3 estimate is the out-of-sample performance of a NOISY SELECTION PROCEDURE, not the population best-in-class value, so the learner-minus-L3 difference is not a difference from the population target and must not be called regret.
L3.learner_ineligibility: If the posterior policy itself fails the +-30 % calibration envelope, C HAS NO COMPARABLE LEARNER RESULT and must say so. The policy must NOT simply drop out of L3's eligible set while any domination or regret statement continues to be made about the remaining eleven: that would quietly restore the invalid e5f779a construction.

regret_language.permitted_when: the difference from the POPULATION target is explicitly estimated or bounded -- for example by correcting the selection bias, or by a bound that holds uniformly over the twelve members
regret_language.not_provided_by: the diagnostic envelope, which is selected on the same sample it is scored on and is therefore optimistically biased downward; using it as a stand-in for the population target would understate regret by exactly the amount of that bias
regret_language.status: no such estimate or bound is attempted in C; regret language is unavailable

L4.name: globally optimal dynamic controller
L4.licenses: 'oracle', 'optimal' and unqualified regret claims require this and it is not attempted; no C result may use those words

falsifier.hard: The DIAGNOSTIC ENVELOPE cannot exceed the learner's worst case in the evaluation sample, because the learner is one of the quantities minimised over. If it does, that is impossible under correct execution and diagnoses Monte-Carlo bookkeeping, a seed mistake or an eligibility bug.
falsifier.not_a_falsifier: The L3 ESTIMATE losing to the learner is NOT a falsifier. It is a possible and interpretable outcome: selecting on finite data can pick a worse member. Reported as selection instability, with the selection-stream and evaluation-stream numbers both shown.
falsifier.corrected_from: bb102d3 attached the hard falsifier to the L3 estimate, where it does not hold.

seeds.why: the schedule that wins is chosen on noise it is not then measured against; evaluation reuses roadmap B's stream so L1, L2 and L3 are measured on the same realisations

required_diagnostics.why: A policy can be nominally adaptive and behaviourally constant. Pooled action frequencies hide that: a policy that reads mid-fringe in every long-tau_c run and the extremum in every short-tau_c run has the same pooled mixture as one that alternates at random, and both differ from one that simply always picks the extremum. The diagnostics must be able to tell those apart, so nothing is aggregated away.

null_stream: action frequency by OPERATING POINT, calibration replicate and seed stream
the posterior over the bank's components through the run -- the filter's hypotheses, which exist under H0 even though no true tau_c does
per-run switch counts, tie counts and their resolutions
post_change_stream: action frequency by TRUE tau_c, which exists only here
per-run switch counts, tie counts and their resolutions
the posterior weights at the moment of each switch, so a switch can be attributed to inference rather than to noise
store.stratification_caveat: Any null grouping aligned with a later tau_c experiment is an EVALUATION STRATUM -- a bookkeeping label matching null runs to the post-change runs they will be compared with -- and never a physical tau_c. It must be named as a stratum wherever it appears.

required_diagnostics.acceptance: Applies to POST-CHANGE behaviour specifically, and with an INTERVAL, not a bare floor. Report the contrast f(tau_c=20) - f(tau_c=1) per policy with replicate-level uncertainty. A 1 percentage-point floor is a sanity check, NOT a statistical test: a 3.6 pp observed spread at R = 32 has a 95 % interval of [-0.7, 7.8] and does not resolve. If the contrast does not resolve, behavioural adaptation is UNDEMONSTRATED -- which is different from absent -- and no feedback claim may be made. Null-stream switching is never evidence of adaptation: under H0 there is nothing to adapt to.
required_diagnostics.null_has_no_tau_c: Under H0 there IS no tau_c: arl_of passes true_tcc=None and run_batch uses it only in the non-null branch. Grouping null diagnostics 'by tau_c' would be meaningless. What does exist under H0 is the BANK's tau_c components as the filter's hypotheses, and the posterior over them still moves because it is fitting noise -- which is precisely what determines the policy's null run length and therefore its calibration.

greedy_posterior_expected_rate.status: retained as a negative baseline; NOT retired
greedy_posterior_expected_rate.why_retained: the R=8 evidence that appeared to disqualify it did not survive independent confirmation: its stress-point action-frequency contrast is 3.6 pp [-0.7, 7.8], unresolved rather than absent

posterior_sampling.why: this policy was designed after seeing the greedy policy's behaviour, and has itself been exercised at R=8 and R=32 on design seeds. Its calibration and delay study can be preregistered prospectively -- they have not been run -- but the POLICY was chosen with knowledge of scouting results and that must not be presented as a blind prediction.
posterior_sampling.rng: a separate action stream, PCG64 via default_rng, reseeded from action_seed at n == 0, never drawing from the latent-process or measurement RNG inside run_batch

supported_now: posterior sampling produces more BALANCED action mixtures than greedy (near 50/50 versus 90/10 at the pilot) -- directly observed
provisional: 'more responsive' -- sampling's contrast resolves at both operating points while greedy's does not at the stress point, but this is design evidence at R = 32 with an uncalibrated threshold
not_implied_by_either: better detection. Neither balance nor responsiveness implies a shorter delay, which is what the calibrated study measures.

identity_separation.why: An earlier version put the realised action seed inside the policy digest. L3 then named policies built with the DESIGN seed 5150, while that seed is excluded from measurement -- so any measurement would have produced a different digest and the measured learner would not have been the learner preregistered in L3. The class membership that makes L3's falsifier work would have failed silently.
identity_separation.policy_identity: decision rule, rate table, operating point, RNG algorithm and the SEED SCHEDULE RULE. The realised seed is excluded, so the policy is the same object under any seed family.
identity_separation.run_identity: the policy digest plus the actual action and data seeds
identity_separation.requirement: calibration, selection and evaluation must not share an action seed, and none may reuse a design seed -- otherwise the policy would be measured on a stream it was tuned against, or a benchmark selected on the stream it is scored on
